sections.content: How many people are "housekeepers and related occupations"?

79,235 people

were counted on the census as "housekeepers and related occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Housekeepers and related workers perform domestic cleaning and other housekeeping tasks within private households, hotels, schools, hostels and other non-private households.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "housekeepers and related occupations" there were more women than men (89% compared with 11%).

This means "housekeepers and related occupations" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "leisure, travel and related personal service occupations".

Men made up 10.9% and women made up 89.1% of "housekeepers and related occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "housekeepers and related occupations" included:

  • typists and related keyboard occupations
  • educational support assistants
  • playworkers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "housekeepers and related occupations" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "housekeepers and related occupations", 15.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "housekeepers and related occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "housekeepers and related occupations" included:

  • upholsterers
  • launderers, dry cleaners and pressers
  • painters and decorators

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "housekeepers and related occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "housekeepers and related occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "housekeepers and related occupations", 11.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (65.3% compared with 34.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (87.2%) than self-employed (12.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
